# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤙 👏 🤌 🤌 👏 🤞 🖐]

I can see the complete initial bomb state: display `0`, blue light, a large button labeled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and three wires in order blue, green, yellow. I cannot hear the Mute’s gesture message, so it has no interpretable meaning for me without an established code. I will report the visible details to both teammates so the Mute can apply the manual and instruct the Blind.

```text
speak(text="Bomb view: display 0. Indicator light blue. Large button reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires, left to right: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟]

The bomb has not visibly changed. The Mute has sent me two gestures, but no gesture meanings have been established, so I cannot safely interpret them. The key path is for the Mute to use the manual together with my bomb description and give the Blind precise spoken instructions; the Blind is the only one who can operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret the gestures without an agreed code. Use the manual with my bomb description, then tell Blind the exact safe action.")
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Mute must provide the manual-based action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👇 👇]

The bomb remains unchanged. I can see the Mute’s three downward gestures, but no code has assigned them a meaning, so they cannot safely convey an instruction. I should not invent a defusal action; the Mute must translate the manual’s requirements into a spoken instruction for the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see three downward gestures, but their meaning is not established. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Please give Blind the exact manual-based instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="No change and no verified action instruction yet. Do not operate the bomb.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged: display `0`, blue light, large “PUSH TO DEFUSE” button, and wires blue, green, yellow from left to right. No new message arrived. I cannot determine the correct action from the bomb’s appearance alone, so I will not invent one; the Mute must consult the manual and verbally direct the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No new message. Visible state remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Please consult the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.")
speak(to="blind", text="No verified action has arrived. Do not press or cut anything until Mute gives a manual-based instruction.")
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 👇 👇 👇]

The bomb remains unchanged. I see four gestures from the Mute, but their meanings have not been established, so I cannot safely decode them. The Mute already has my complete visual description and must use the manual to give the Blind a direct spoken instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode the four gestures without an agreed mapping. Please speak the manual-based instruction directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains unchanged. Wait for Mute's exact spoken instruction based on the manual; do not operate it yet.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged. The Mute sent one gesture, but no meaning has been assigned to that gesture. Since the Mute cannot speak, I should report the gesture’s observable form to the Blind and ask the Mute to encode a clear instruction using an agreed scheme rather than relying on unexplained signs.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No bomb change: display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires blue green yellow. Mute just signalled one gesture: index and little fingers raised, other fingers folded, thumb across the middle fingers. Its meaning is unknown.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the single gesture with index and little fingers raised. Its meaning is not established. Please use a clearly agreed gesture code to convey the manual instruction; I will speak the decoded instruction to Blind.")
```
